Mental health can change over time, with different patterns of symptoms and well-being. We describe these trajectories in study populations and investigate the social, family and individual contexts associated with them.
Trabalhamos sobretudo com dados longitud: We work mainly with longitudinal data — following the same people over time — because this helps distinguish one-off changes from persistent patterns. The 2019 Rio Grande Birth Cohort is one of the group's main platforms for this kind of research.
Queremos também identificar momentos e c: We also want to identify moments and contexts in which prevention, care and support may be especially relevant.

Álcool e saúde mental durante a pandemia: Alcohol and mental health during the pandemic
5% das mães relataram aumento do consumo: 5% of mothers reported drinking more alcohol during the pandemic; in this group, depression and anxiety scores were higher.
Isso não mostra que o álcool tenha causa: This does not show that alcohol caused these symptoms, but it indicates that changes in drinking can accompany periods of greater psychological distress.
Durante o isolamento, 51,9% das mães rel: During isolation, 51.9% of mothers reported less physical activity and 58.1% said they had increased the amount of food they ate.
Numa crise, hábitos como alimentação e a: In a crisis, everyday habits such as eating and physical activity also deserve attention in mothers’ health.
Sono na gestação e sintomas de depressão: Sleep in pregnancy and symptoms of depression and anxiety
Menor duração do sono, dificuldade para: Shorter sleep, difficulty falling asleep or getting up and a more evening-type sleep pattern were associated with more symptoms of depression and/or anxiety.
Observar o sono pode ajudar a reconhecer: Looking at sleep can help recognise situations of greater emotional vulnerability in the perinatal period.
Ter dados anteriores à crise permitiu di: Data collected before the crisis allowed us to measure the change in maternal mental health rather than describe a single point in time.
Depressão e ansiedade ao longo da pandem: Depression and anxiety throughout the pandemic
Entre as mães avaliadas nos três momento: Among mothers assessed at all three time points, depression rose from 3.1% before the pandemic to 30.6% at the second assessment during the pandemic; anxiety rose from 9.6% to 28.8%.
Seguir as mesmas mulheres ao longo do te: Following the same women over time showed the scale of the change and illustrates the strength of a cohort for studying what happens during a crisis.
